summary: Tested the CloudIVR onboarding redesign from end to end, on the backend and in the browser at 1920 and 390 wide. Everything requested works. Backend: 16 of 16 pytest tests pass, covering journey events (whitelist, anonymous and signed-in, chatId stored), register source/marketing opt-in/signupDevice, PUT /prefs/email marketing, and PUT /prefs/onboarding with new and legacy ids. UI: I signed up a new account after landing with ?utm_source=testsrc&utm_campaign=c1. The marketing checkbox is unticked by default and the policy box is required (submit is blocked without it). The DB shows source {utm_source:testsrc, utm_campaign:c1, landing:/cloudivr/}. The onboarding dialog shows 'What do you need?' with all 7 purposes. Picking travel+texting -> Continue -> 'Go to my Overview' shows no profile-setup-dialog. Home has dashboard-purpose-home with the travel and texting cards, and their primary links go to /app/travel-esim and /app/texting-number. 'Change what I need' reopens the dialog with the old picks still selected. The dashboard-for-you strip is not shown. The desktop sidebar has the 5 groups (home has no heading), all 27 old nav testids exist, and the 12 I clicked route correctly with aria-current=page. The mobile More menu shows the Numbers/Messaging/Calls & AI/Account groups. Home is not a More group because it is in the bottom tabs. The Settings marketing toggle showed off after signup, flipped to on, and stayed on after reload; webAccounts.marketingOptIn was updated. Buying a number on the new account shows buy-profile-gate after picking a number and no Checkout. Travel eSIM: with no search 40 countries show plus the hint; show-all reveals 187. A dry-run UK 1GB $6 order showed the date text 'Bought 11/14/2026 · valid 2 days after you first connect · preview order (not real)' and the QR placeholder 'Preview order — no real QR code'. The travel_esim_paid event was stored. All test data was cleaned up.

minor.issue: This route is public and has no rate limit and no TTL/retention index, so anyone can flood the webEvents collection. Props are capped at 12 keys x 300 chars, but the number of requests is not.

integration_issues.issue: In preview, each route change logs page_view twice (e.g. /cloudivr/app twice right after signup). Cause: React.StrictMode in index.js runs the Shell useEffect twice in dev. Production builds are not affected, but preview analytics are inflated. page_view also only fires inside the app Shell, so the landing page and the signup page are not tracked (only signup_started).

issues: The buy-profile-gate card sits flush against the bottom of the plan cards, with almost no gap.
The copy button for the manual activation code is pushed to the far right edge, far from the code, because the code span is flex-1.

action_items: Optional: add a per-IP rate limit and a TTL index (e.g. 180 days on 'at') for webEvents.
Optional: track page_view for public pages (landing/signup) if funnel analysis needs them. Duplicates in preview come from StrictMode; consider deduping by pathname in track.
Minor spacing: add a top margin above BuyProfileGate; put the travel eSIM copy button next to the code.
critical_code_review_comments: EmailPrefs Toggle uses checked={prefs[k] !== false}. For 'marketing' this would show ON if the server ever omitted the key. It is safe today because the server merges DEFAULTS (marketing:false), but it is fragile for an opt-in field and should use === true for marketing.
auth.js register: marketingOptIn is accepted only when it is strictly true. Verified that 'yes' is stored as false. Good.
sourceOf whitelist correctly drops unknown keys and the client 'at' timestamp. Verified.
seed_data_creation: None kept. I created test_iter275_* accounts (pytest plus 1 UI signup, test_iter275_ui_1794686141@example.com) and purged them by id: webAccounts, webPrefs, walletOf, state, nameOf, compliance, legalAcceptances and their webEvents. I made 1 Travel eSIM dry-run order tes_70d02ab8-10c for civr.uxtest; I deleted it and its transaction travel-esim-tes_70d02ab8-10c and refunded $6 (wallet back to $784.65).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Web accounts live in the webAccounts collection (_id is stored as a double, e.g. 5000000000000077.0). Other collections use str(int(_id)). civr.uxtest chatId = 5000000000000077. Register is limited to 15 sign-ups per IP per 15 minutes; this run used about 12. The Travel eSIM zone testid is lowercase-hyphenated (travel-esim-zone-united-kingdom) and the pay button is travel-esim-pay-button. The pytest purge() helper in the iter275 test file cleans up a created account fully.
